clue.text: European wife preceding husband

indicators.note: the first piece comes before the second, so the wife's word is set in front

parts.note: 'old Dutch' is cockney slang for a wife
man is an informal word for a husband, as in 'man and wife'

explanation.surface: A continental wife walks ahead of her husband.
explanation.walkthrough: DUTCH for wife comes from the cockney 'my old Dutch' (Dutch from 'duchess'), a London slang term.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of the Netherlands is a European.

clue.text: Some of the French are unable to sing this way

parts.note: des is French for 'some of the'
can't means are unable

explanation.surface: Some French people cannot sing in a certain style.
explanation.definitionFit: A counter-melody sung above the main tune is a style of singing.

clue.text: Light score

explanation.surface: A small tally in a game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Light' means to alight or land, as a plane does; the second sense is a scoring play in rugby or American football.
explanation.definitionFit: Landing an aircraft is alighting; grounding the ball over the line earns points in American football and rugby.

clue.text: Hard speech cut in Shakespearian part

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

indicators.note: cut means the speech's word loses its final letter

parts.note: an oration is a formal speech

explanation.surface: A tough speech is trimmed in a Shakespeare role.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' removes the last letter N from ORATION; the held clue had lost its last two words to the column break.
explanation.definitionFit: Hamlet's loyal friend is a character in Shakespeare's play.

clue.text: Lack never experienced by people here

definitions.text: Lack never experienced by people here

parts.words: Lack never experienced by people here
parts.note: people who are here are present, so they can never experience the state of being away

explanation.definitionFit: Being away is a lack of presence, which those present cannot know.

clue.text: Provide inspiration for puzzle

explanation.surface: Someone is asked to be a source of ideas for a crossword setter.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as BE MUSE, the first part means to serve as someone's inspiration; run together it means to bewilder.
explanation.definitionFit: To be a muse is to inspire an artist; to bemuse is to confuse or bewilder.

clue.text: Darling nonetheless goes on ahead to pavilion

indicators.note: the word for ahead goes on after the first piece
read as none-the-less, it says the word for darling loses its 'none', an O

parts.note: a beloved is a darling
ere is an old word for before, ahead in time

explanation.surface: A loved one nevertheless walks ahead to the cricket pavilion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nonetheless' is read as none-the-less: the darling word loses its 'none', the letter O, as nought. 'goes on' puts the word for ahead after it. 'pavilion' here is a garden summer-house, not a cricket one.
explanation.definitionFit: A summer-house or gazebo built to command a view is a garden pavilion.

clue.text: State Helena is always in

parts.note: reads like a woman named Helena forever being in some mood, but Helena is a US state capital that never moves

explanation.definitionFit: Helena is the capital city of this western US state.

clue.text: Fliers' short time in stormy skies

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation for time inside the rearranged skies
stormy suggests turbulence, so the letters of skies are churned

parts.note: hr is the short form of hour

explanation.surface: Birds have only a brief spell in a turbulent sky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stormy' rearranges SKIES, and 'in' puts HR inside; the apostrophe in 'Fliers'' stands for 'have'.
explanation.definitionFit: Butcher-birds are predatory songbirds, so they are fliers.

clue.text: Fogeys have trouble with some canvas

parts.note: old-fashioned, conventional people are squares
to ail is to be troubled or unwell

explanation.surface: Old fuddy-duddies struggle when putting up a tent.
explanation.definitionFit: A square sail is a four-sided sail of canvas, so it is a piece of a ship's canvas.

clue.text: An extreme of nationalism is nothing unusual

annotationWithheld.why: An extreme of nationalism is nothing unusual (4): the wordplay reads 'an extreme of nationalism' as N OR M (either end letter), which no form of the grammar can express without supplying OR from no clue word
annotationWithheld.clue: An extreme of nationalism is nothing unusual

clue.text: Guess it's no cooler at night

explanation.surface: A remark that the evening brings no relief from the heat.
explanation.walkthrough: The second part reads as A'S HOT IN THE DARK: 'no cooler' means it is hot, and 'at night' means in the dark.
explanation.definitionFit: A wild guess made without information is called a shot fired blindly in darkness.

clue.text: Game couple

explanation.surface: Two people up for anything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Game' looks like an adjective meaning willing; it is a noun, a golf match between two players.
explanation.definitionFit: In golf a singles match between two players has this name; a couple is a pair of people.

clue.text: Trader's centre on island

parts.note: the middle is the centre
the Isle of Man is an island in the Irish Sea

explanation.surface: A merchant's base is on an island.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A dealer buying from producers and selling on is an intermediary trader.

clue.text: Sign of renewed ill feeling

parts.note: reads like resentment flaring up again between people, but 'ill feeling' means feeling unwell, and its return is a medical setback

explanation.definitionFit: A patient's falling back into sickness after improving is a return of ill health.

clue.text: Tommy King's warship

parts.note: Tommy Atkins is slang for a British private soldier
ER, Edwardus Rex, is a king's royal cipher

explanation.surface: A British soldier boards the monarch's man-of-war.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tommy' is British slang for an ordinary soldier, the rank of private.
explanation.definitionFit: An armed privately owned ship licensed to attack enemy shipping served as a warship.

clue.text: Do this in panic, once defeated?

definitions.text: Do this in panic, once defeated?

indicators.note: the letters needed sit inside the run of words panic, once defeated

explanation.surface: Advice on what to do when beaten and flustered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' tells you the answer sits inside 'paniC ONCE DEfeated'; the whole clue also describes the act, admitting defeat once beaten.
explanation.definitionFit: Giving in or admitting defeat is what someone does once beaten.

clue.text: Veteran replaced in New Deal

indicators.note: replaced in says one word in the phrase is swapped for its opposite

parts.note: taken as written
a deal in cards is a hand dealt to a player

explanation.surface: A veteran is swapped out in Roosevelt's New Deal.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'Deal' as a hand of cards to get NEW HAND, then 'replaced in' swaps NEW for its opposite OLD.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone long experienced at a job is a seasoned practitioner, a veteran.

clue.text: Instruction in preparing menus

explanation.surface: Guidance for planning meals.
explanation.walkthrough: One sense is classes of teaching; the other is the dishes, starter to dessert, that a menu is built from.
explanation.definitionFit: A series of lessons is a programme of study; a meal's successive dishes are what a menu lists.

clue.text: Adorning one centrepiece after a month

indicators.note: the chess piece's word follows the month's abbreviation

parts.note: Dec is the short form of December
the king is the central piece of a chess set, the one the whole game revolves around

explanation.surface: Someone is decorating a table with a single central ornament a month later.
explanation.walkthrough: 'centrepiece' suggests table decoration; here it means the most important piece in chess.
explanation.definitionFit: To deck is to decorate, so decking means decorating.

clue.text: Song about an old herbal remedy

indicators.note: about means the word for song goes around the other piece

parts.note: a ditty is a short simple song
taken as written

explanation.surface: A tune about a traditional plant cure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'old' belongs to the definition: the herb was a remedy in ancient times, not an old word in the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: This aromatic plant of Crete was used for centuries as a healing herb.

clue.text: Argument against one match or another

parts.note: con means against, as in pros and cons
a test is one sort of match, as in cricket's Test matches

explanation.surface: A dispute against one game or another.
explanation.definitionFit: A dispute or struggle between rivals is a fight over something, an argument.

clue.text: Got idea worked out in plant

indicators.note: worked out suggests the letters are reworked into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: An idea is formed while standing in a garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worked out' rearranges GOT and IDEA.
explanation.definitionFit: This annual is a flowering garden plant, also called clarkia.

clue.text: Bad rule — adds no end of resentment, perhaps

definitions.text: Bad rule — adds no end of resentment, perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps hints the letters might be arranged some other way, so they are mixed up
end of picks the final letter of resentment

explanation.surface: An unfair rule only stokes resentment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges BADRULE ADDS NO plus T, the last letter of 'resentment' picked out by 'end of'; the whole clue also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A rule applied unequally to different people is a bad rule that breeds resentment.

clue.text: It's found in S.E. Asia, also in other places

indicators.note: letters put in other places are moved around, so the word also is rearranged

explanation.surface: Something native to Southeast Asia turns up elsewhere too.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in other places' rearranges ALSO; the held text had puzzle-header debris tacked onto the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: This landlocked country lies in Southeast Asia, between Thailand and Vietnam.

clue.text: Board's trickery

explanation.surface: Sharp practice by a company's directors.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', linking the two senses.
explanation.definitionFit: A company's directors collectively are its bosses; the word also once meant artful handling or contrivance.

clue.text: Not even child can be such a favourite

parts.note: a number that is not even is odd
a son is a male child

explanation.surface: An uneven child is tipped to win.
explanation.definitionFit: A runner priced shorter than evens is the strong favourite in betting.

clue.text: Is intoxicated with hearty over-excitement

indicators.note: someone intoxicated is all over the place, so the letters of the two words are jumbled

explanation.surface: Drunk and hearty, someone gets far too worked up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'intoxicated' rearranges IS and HEARTY together.
explanation.definitionFit: Uncontrolled emotional frenzy is extreme over-excitement.
